elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment..."; the prior USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay language is deleted, and § 12.3's acknowledgement of no minimum-volume commitment is retained consistently.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "...and pays only for usage or Services ordered under an Order Form," consistent with the § 1.7 definition of Services (described in an Order Form) and § 7.1's Order Form fee construct.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No commitment survives in the rendered § 2.1, so no 12-month-term limitation language exists; the fallback checklist is not the level pursued.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text contains no reduction-on-notice mechanic; the 30 days' notice fallback is only mentioned in the margin comment, which is not operative.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: No shortfall or true-up mechanic appears in the rendered language (none is needed given no commitment remains).

reasons: Preferred level is complete: rendered § 2.1 states both that Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment and that Customer pays only for usage or Services ordered under an Order Form.

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original § 2.1 was a three-year take-or-pay with express denial of reduction or termination rights and no true-up, which fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory.

Minimal: the edit is confined to replacing the single offending sentence in § 2.1; no survival tails, damages categories, notice procedures, or other extras were added, and § 12.3's favourable acknowledgement was left untouched.

Preserves intent: the replacement uses the defined terms Services and Order Form, aligns with § 7.1's Order Form fee construct, removes the contradiction with § 12.3, and leaves no dangling cross-reference or orphaned shortfall/true-up reference.

Fallback elements are unmet only because the drafter targeted the preferred level; the fallback is offered in the comment, which is appropriate and does not affect completeness at the preferred level.
